ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Frederick Douglass Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing care with a trauma-informed intake: right-hand pain and stiffness with writing, short and broken sleep, and screening for trauma-related symptoms with his consent at each step. Concerns: His right hand aches and stiffens after about an hour of writing, and holding a pen has grown harder over the past year; he writes for his living and wants to keep doing it; He sleeps about five hours on working nights, has nightmares about his youth once or twice a month, and asked whether anything can help him sleep; He wants care that respects his history without making it the whole of who he is; he chooses what to tell and agreed to answer screening questions about past violence. [S]

tr.td: Diclofenac 1% gel, 2 g to the right hand up to four times a day
2 g rubbed into the back and palm of the right hand up to four times a day, including before long writing sessions

Plain X-ray of the right hand, three views, with his consent: healed fractures of the fourth and fifth metacarpal shafts with about 20 degrees of angulation and shortening of the fifth; joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, and subchondral sclerosis at the fourth and fifth metacarpophalangeal joints; no erosions; other joints normal

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Collapse with violent headache, dizziness, and trembling while working in the August heat, followed by kicks and a blow to the head
Kick to the left eye in an assault at a Baltimore shipyard; the eye was closed and badly swollen
Broken right hand in a mob assault; the bones were not properly set, and the hand did not recover its natural strength and dexterity

tr.td: Establishing care with a trauma-informed intake: right-hand pain and stiffness with writing, short and broken sleep, and screening for trauma-related symptoms with his consent at each step
Two-week review of the hand and sleep, with clinical psychology evaluation the same day
Ten-week review after hand therapy and two sleep sessions
Five-month review of the hand, sleep, and trauma-related symptoms
Same-day sick visit for hoarseness after a cold and several talks

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Referral to clinical psychology for a trauma-informed diagnostic evaluation of nightmares, watchfulness, and short sleep, with trauma-focused psychotherapy (cognitive processing therapy or prolonged exposure) offered if he meets criteria for PTSD and wants it

Trauma-informed care at every visit: explain each question, examination, and test before it happens and ask his agreement; offer a chaperone; let him choose what to share and stop at any time; no retelling of details is needed for his care
Measurement-based follow-up: PCL-5 and PHQ-9 at each chronic-care visit and hand pain on a 0 to 10 scale at every visit

Hand care: diclofenac 1% gel up to four times a day; six sessions with a hand therapist over eight weeks for range-of-motion and strengthening exercises and joint protection; a wide-barrel pen, a ten-minute break each hour of writing, and dictation for long drafts
A care plan built on the strengths he names: his work and writing, his family and community, and his faith, with visits scheduled around his travel for speaking

Brief behavioral treatment for insomnia in two sessions with Dr. Morrison: a fixed waking time, a seven-hour sleep window, no writing in the last hour before bed, a short routine for nights after a nightmare, and a two-week sleep diary
Write for an hour with right-hand pain no higher than 2 of 10
Met at ten weeks: pain 2 of 10 after an hour of writing
Sleep at least seven hours on five nights a week
Met at five months: about seven hours on five or six nights a week; nightmares about once a month
Track trauma-related symptoms with the PCL-5 and return to psychology if the score reaches the probable-PTSD range or he wants treatment
PCL-5 24, 19, and 16; no return needed so far
Every examination, test, and question about his history happens only with his agreement
Consent recorded at every visit; he declined a back examination at intake, and the offer stays open

list.item: Independent in all activities; writing limited to about an hour at a stretch by right-hand pain and stiffness [S]
